utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Joanna Korner, Ann Sutherland, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning to you. Appearances for Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour I'm John Ackerman, I'm here today with Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning. We have a new witness. Before we bring the witness in are there any preliminary statements?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I return to the point that Your Honour raised on Friday? That is in relation to the judicial notice in respect of the Jaskici killings and I had an opportunity of reading Mr. Ackerman's response and as I said to him this morning, it was always nice to be able to quote yourself in support of a proposition that you're making even though the proposition was of your own making. However, Your Honour, although as I said last time it seems to me that by doing -- by handing over all the transcripts, we are negating Rule 94 but as yet nobody seems to have used Rule 94. However, we have already disclosed during the course of our disclosure three witnesses who dealt with those killings. Mr. Ackerman is already in possession of that. I won't read the names aloud and we will disclose the other three at the end of today. So that Mr. Ackerman can see on what we base or on what the Appeals Chamber based its finding. I said in error that these were protected witnesses. They weren't, and so with one exception there is a document that was filed confidentially, contained the names of the people killed or beaten. Your Honour, of course the rule has changed so we wouldn't have to apply to Judge Jorda but to you if Mr. Ackerman requires to have it. I don't however feel that he's possibly very interested in the list of names but anyhow, Your Honour, that will be supplied to Mr. Ackerman, all six witnesses who dealt with this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My assumption is that Ms. Korner is speaking of transcripts not witness statements because that's what the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. I have one very brief matter Your Honour just for -- first of all let me just respond very briefly to what Ms. Korner said. I believe when I file a pleading with this Chamber, that I have an obligation to provide you with the most authoritative sources and so that's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You understand that, yeah. On Friday, this is a document report, Your Honour. On Friday, 8 November, we received an additional 826 pages of Prijedor witness material at 2 minutes per page this works out to 27 and a half hours of reading time. Since October 24th, we've received 1.955 pages of new witness material. This does not include documents, just witness material. This works out to 122 pages per day of reading.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you slow down, Mr. Ackerman, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. It works out to 122 pages per day of daily reading time of four hours each day. So the numbers that I gave you last week are not complete. It's been significantly added to just this last Friday. And so that's what we are facing and I just wanted to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. The next witness has not asked for any protective measures, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, he hasn't, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's bring in Mr. Merdzanic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Doctor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Dr. Merdzanic. Do you think you'll finish with this witness today, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, yes, Your Honour. I would imagine I'll finish before the break because he testified very recently in Stakic. Your Honour, I will refer Your Honours to the page numbers in the transcript that deal with the various matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. That's perfect. Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think we can finish today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And after this witness, do you have anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I don't Your Honour. Your Honour will recall that we had to substitute at the last moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm flying home tomorrow and if you had another witness, I was trying to shift the afternoon sitting to the morning so that we could have -- you could have the full time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I think Mr. Ackerman will be given an extra day to look at matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, doctor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome to this Tribunal again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand you have already given evidence in the Stakic case so I will be very succinct, very short in my address to you. Before you start giving evidence, the rules require that you enter a solemn declaration, the text of which you have in your hand at the moment. And that will be your undertaking to this Tribunal that in the course of your testimony, you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Sit down. I think we can skip the preliminaries you're already familiar to this kind of courtroom. I'm the Presiding Judge, my name is Agius and I am flanked on my right by Judge Janu from the Czech Republic and my left Judge Taya from Japan. The three of us constitute this Trial Chamber. To your right you have the team for the Prosecution headed by Ms. Joanna Korner. I don't know who will be conducting the chief, who will be putting some questions to you this morning. And to your left, there is the team for Radoslav Brdjanin, who is the accused in this trial. The lead counsel is Mr. John Ackerman who presumably will conduct the cross-examination. So what's going to happen is that we are going to take as read, sort of, the -- are you receiving the interpretation? We are going to take as read your previous testimony but there will be some additional questions from the Prosecution and a full cross-examination on the part of the Defence. Having said that, I leave you in the hands of Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dr. Merdzanic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dr. Merdzanic, can I just establish again your details for the purpose of the record? Is your name Idriz Merdzanic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I'm Idriz Merdzanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you a medical doctor by profession?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. I graduated from the faculty, Banja Luka, and after being a trainee, I -- and then intern, I worked as a general practitioner in Prijedor in the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think it's right that you were born on the 2nd of January of 1959, so that you're now aged 43?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone or speak up?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dr. Merdzanic, could you come -- or pull -- somebody is going to come and help you. And doctor, I think it's right that by nationality you're a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At the time of the attack that took place in May of 1992 in Kozarac, on Kozarac, were you working as a medical doctor in Trnopolje and in Kozarac itself?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's right. At that time, I worked in Trnopolje and Kozarac. Or to be more accurate, in Kozarac I would do duty shifts and then I had a workers infirmary at the sawmill.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you living, however, at the time, in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I was living in Prijedor, yes. I lived there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think just to set in context as well, you appeared first at this Tribunal on the 10th and 11th of September, so almost exactly two months ago, when you testified in the case of the Prosecutor against Milomir Stakic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we deal first straight away with this accused, Radoslav Brdjanin? I think it's right that you never met him?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I didn't, no. I do not know Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Never saw him in the camp in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I did not see him in the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Had you ever before the events of May, 1992, seen him on television?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I can't be quite sure. I wouldn't be able to say yes or no. Perhaps I did see him on television at some point but I didn't pay much attention. I'd heard that there was a Brdjanin who held some political office in the SDS but I didn't pay any attention.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think as you told the Court before, you had very little, if any, interest in politics?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want -- I'm going to ask you this morning to look again at a number of photographs and some video clips which you looked at before so that the Judges can hear your explanation of them but I want to put them into context. Now, first, can we deal with showing the whereabouts of Kozarac in relation to others? Could you look, please, at a map and then we'll look at your own drawing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour I'm not sure Your Honours have got this with one yet. You have, thank you have much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have it, Ms. Korner, but of course it shows an exhibit number which --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'll give you a clean one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have it and I've been told to keep everything in this plastic bag by my secretary, not even to take them out of the plastic bag but apparently they come from the other case and I think they have to go back or something like that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, Your Honour, but of course we did copies with the Stakic number on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes exactly because it says Exhibit 146 and the date admitted and it's in ink so unless it's a colour photocopy, which shows the ink.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've acquired the representative of the Registry today from the Stakic case so she can help out with anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, would Your Honours be kind enough to mark this P1146? And could -- yes, the witness has got it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is there a copy for us?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly not. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we see, doctor, marked on that the position of Kozarac which I think it lies on a junction with the road between Prijedor and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is Kozarac. Kozarac is right where I'm pointing at. There is a junction, a road leading to Trnopolje, which is rather poorly marked but that was a road -- it wasn't a dirt road and it went to Trnopolje and then there was another road going through Kozarac to Kozara, where there was a hotel and a TV relay station, a transmitter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can see that Trnopolje was very close to the railway line that went Prijedor, Trnopolje, Omarska?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The railway tracks was skirting Trnopolje and there was a small railway station there too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: After Omarska, where did the railway go to? What was the next station, do you know?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Before Banja Luka, there were some other railway stations but I can't really give you all their names but they were several stations before Banja Luka. I wouldn't be able to give you their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did the railway, that particular railway line, end in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: In Banja Luka and from Banja Luka, of course, you could then proceed to Doboj and in the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Okay. You can put that plan away now. Now, can we look, please, next at the sketch that you did of the Kozarac area? Because that shows a number of things.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are going to be a number of sketch plans so I'd like them all collected together as it were under one exhibit number so could we have that as P1147.1? Which for identification purposes has got the ERN number 01035313.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. What you've marked there, I think, is again the main road between Prijedor and Banja Luka, which you say was asphalt. What have you marked below the word "Prijedor"? What does that show us?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It says, "Tavern, coffee shop." When they were taking us from Kozarac to Trnopolje, here from a military jeep we got off the military jeep at this place and changed to buses.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then you've marked on to -- as we go up Kozarac, and I think the road runs up the -- towards from the main road towards some hills; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: You mean this one which is northward and goes through Kozarac? Yes. You are right, it goes uphill and then towards Kozara mount. A hotel that was up on the mountain and a big TV transmitter was also in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then if we just move from the Prijedor road as one goes up it to the left there is the sawmill?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's right. Right at the junction, there is a sawmill on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then moving up towards the centre, was there a veterinary clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The veterinary clinic was next, adjacent to the sawmill, where it says Veterinarska Stanica, veterinary station, that is where the veterinary station was. And then the first road to the left leads to the infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in the veterinary clinic, was there a vet named Dr. Azra Blazevic working?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Azra Blazevic worked there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as you told the Court on the last occasion, and as we are going to see shortly in the photographs, she was with you in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Correct. Not only in Trnopolje. He [sic] was in Kozarac throughout with us again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we go, still going up the road, we see the centre of Kozarac and is that where you were taken to when the soldiers arrived?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I marked it as a centre but basically, the centre of Kozarac is somewhere between this junction and then upward. All this was perceived as the centre because it's a small place but this junction is where the soldiers had brought us from the infirmary to this place, and we covered this distance on foot before we were put on the military jeep.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then going up the road still we see the pharmacy. Was that where you attempted to get medical supplies after Kozarac was shut off?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: From this pharmacy, we transferred all the medicines, all the supplies to the infirmary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then still going further up, we see the temporary clinic. Was that where you moved to once the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: We moved there one day after the shelling. The shelling began on the 24th, I think it was about noon, I'm not sure exactly what time it was. The next day on the 25th, we moved to one house which was just under construction. It wasn't finished this house. And the police of Kozarac was already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. If we can come back down the road then, please, so now we are looking at the right of the street, the main street, we see there set back off the road the medical clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. From the crossroads where it says "centre" there is a road leading to the right, and at the end of this road is the medical clinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we are going to look at some photographs of what it looked like after the shelling in a moment but if we come down literally more or less to the -- do we see there you've marked there, is that the Serb Orthodox Church?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The Serb Orthodox Church was south of the medical clinic. This is the road. And there was a turning going down, and then the church was actually in the curve in the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to you look, now, please, at some photographs. Some which you have seen before, some which you haven't. And the first one --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, these are all -- I think a bundle of photographs were put in and it's already -- sorry. It's P1128. I'm told the bundle of photographs is there. We may have to put it up on the ELMO Your Honour because I'm not sure we've got sufficient copies of all of these. Your Honours have only got the ones we used in the Stakic trial and these are some extra ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These have already been -- I recognise the photo as being one of a number of photos exhibited in the course of the testimony of either the previous witness or the one before the last. So you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They have all been tendered as exhibits already.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the whole bundle has been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But each individual --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would Your Honour forgive me one moment. Ms. Sutherland is the queen of these photographs so I just want to check.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Sutherland informed me that last -- the week before last, as each one was admitted they were given a number but it seems to me it's much simpler if we just number them in advance rather than trying to allocate a number each time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What actually happened was this: We were given the whole bundle but not all of them have as yet been tendered as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Those to which reference was being made as we went along have been given a number. The whole set has been given a number, an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the rest is point and so that we would create the sequence but basically the whole set has been given a number already.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can't remember it now, 1 to 8, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right in that case, could I -- could the witness have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The one you have in your hand has already been made use of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, it has, has it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the registry's purpose, the ERN number is 00393467. All right. Can we just put this one on the ELMO, Your Honour, rather than -- usher, can you just put it on the ELMO? Probably be easiest. Thanks. And the next number is 112825. 1128.25.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can you just identify, please, the photographs that we can see? This is a photograph of a postcard. What are we looking at to the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: On the left side is a mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know how many mosques Kozarac had?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: There were many mosques, but I was not so familiar with Kozarac. I knew this road from the road to the medical centre well because I would go to work there, but the rest of Kozarac, I didn't really tour that much but I do know that there were several mosques.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, I think we will show you another photograph in a moment and that will help. Then if we look at the top picture on the right, what are we looking at there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I think that this is Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that looking from the Prijedor road up towards the hills?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The picture is taken from the other -- no. I think it's the other way around. It's from the other side towards the...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Looking towards Prijedor road --

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: But as I said, I'm not so familiar with this part of Kozarac because I only went to Kozarac because of my work so I would go to the medical clinic and back. I don't know the rest of Kozarac so well but I think that this picture was taken from the upper-side, from the Kozara mountain, down towards the Banja Luka-Prijedor crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm not going to press you on this but do you happen to recognise the bottom picture on the right? If you don't, say so, doctor. Don't worry about it.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It's probably also Kozarac but I'm not sure, but I think that this is the Kozarac mosque, when you go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to just put into context -- thank you very much. You can take the photograph away. The next set of photographs I'm going to show you. As you told us, the shelling of Kozarac began on the 24th of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the evidence about that begins on page 7732 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before the shelling began, was there a complete blockade of the town?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The town was blocked first, when the negotiations were conducted between the citizens of Kozarac and the Serb authorities, but it was blocked in such a way that checkpoints were set up around Kozarac and IDs were checked while passing through the checkpoints but it was still possible to pass through. At the moment when the ultimatum was issued for Kozarac to surrender and when the deadline for the ultimatum ran out I think this was on the 22nd, then this tank that was placed at the crossroads withdrew and then only the checkpoints remained at Orlovci [phoen] and from that point on, nobody could leave Kozarac any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were people who were in need of hospital treatment, which was the hospital being Prijedor, were they allowed to pass through the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, from that point on, nobody, not even sick persons, and this was just before the shelling, maybe even on the morning before the shelling took place, two women went into labour and gave birth at the health clinic in Kozarac and they said that they were not allowed to pass through to go to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in fact, did you have to deliver their babies in your clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. I delivered the babies, together with a nurse.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, the shelling, when it started, did that come from the north, from the hills around Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: As far as we were able to notice, they were coming from the north, from the direction of Kozarac and from the west, from the direction of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And again, and I'm summarising the evidence that you gave about this, I think that people were killed and wounded during the course of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's true. They were wounded and killed, people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you attempted to negotiate with the army, to get the wounded -- to evacuate children and wounded?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours this is at page 7737 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you were unsuccessful?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The next day, the 25th, when we moved to this house where the clinic was transferred, we had two small children, a little girl who was maybe ten or 12 years old. Both of her legs were practically severed by the shell. They were just hanging on by a thread. There was also a little boy who could have been eight years old, who had a large wound on his left thigh, upper -- upper leg, and the bone was exposed. There was a lot of bleeding. We had two women also, one of the women died very quickly, the other one was still alive. We also had a man who had a bullet wound in his back. We also had one of their uniformed men, who had an injury -- a wound on his stomach. It was mostly because of the children that I had decided to try to ask them to allow the wounded persons to go to Prijedor. Upstairs was the police. They had a police car, a police vehicle, parked outside, and I asked them whether it was possible to talk to the Serbs. They said that they were manning the radio station and that I could try to do so. I tried to talk. I introduced myself over the radio station. I explained that we had wounded persons, but nobody wanted to talk to me seriously. In principle, they just laughed. You could hear the laughter, and they said something to the effect, "Die, balijas, we are going to kill you any way." We even said that we had one of their wounded and they didn't say anything to that. And after that, they didn't even respond when called on that frequency.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want you now, please, to look at a series of photographs that were taken in respect of your clinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And those, Your Honours, I think in that small bundle they are marked 0039-3914 through to 15, 16 -- I'm sorry, 194, 195, 196 and 198? What happened to 197? All right. Could the witness be handed those now, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, Ms. Korner, shall we give an exhibit number to the witness testimony in Stakic, please? To the document itself?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Sorry, Your Honour. That will be P1148.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. The first one then, could we have it on the ELMO? That's we've got -- all right. 194. What are we looking at there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is the entrance to the medical clinic in Kozarac, to the left is the larger part of the building. This was the entrance. This was where the dental offices were. This is where the dentists worked. Downstairs is the entrance to the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in the basement, was that where you took shelter originally?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's where we took shelter during the shelling and when we saw that upstairs, in the clinic, it was too dangerous, that shrapnel was coming in through the windows so we had to take shelter downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We can see on the wall then, we'll see it again later, there is a circle with a cross in it. Two circles, there were two of these markings. Were those markings on there when you left the clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that the markings were there before, or at the time when we were leaving the clinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are these photographs were taken in 1996. When you left the clinic, was this -- was the damage that we can see there already done?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Most of it was already done. It's true that with the passage of time, the building further deteriorated but it's also evident that the glass was broken by the shrapnel and also the damage on the walls dates from that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look, then, please, at the next one, 3195? I think the same side of the clinic but taken from a bit further back. The house to the left, with all the windows missing, what was that? To the left as we look at it.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Upstairs was the lab. Downstairs, these small windows are windows of the basement. Upstairs there were also doctors' offices, examination rooms, and there was also one room where the doctor on duty could sleep, and then you can also see along, a little further along, some more windows of examination rooms, and then downstairs to the left in the basement was the boiler room for the central heating.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, please, next, could you look at number 3196 very briefly? Because that's just a close-up of the same part of the clinic.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. This is the left part of the building, which can be seen in its entirety on the photograph. You can see traces of shrapnel, the broken windows as well, which was actually the condition of the building at the time when we were leaving it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then finally, on this, number 3198?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the entrance to the courtyard of the clinic, and on the left side you can see the road that leads towards the centre, and down here, the road turns right down towards the Serbian church. I think that there was also a small road here, and there were a couple of houses here that you could come up to. You can see it here but as the shells were falling into the courtyard and there was a parking place there, they were leaving small shells -- craters so there were traces of the shelling left, being left here, but you can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Finally, before we leave the photographs, I think all these photographs were taken from the front. Was the damage in fact greater to the back? Because that was where the shelling was coming from.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I assume that from the north, the damage was greater, because there was no road on the other side. We were not able to go out and look. But when we were up in the clinic, when we were hiding, most of the shells came from the -- from the other side, from up above. So I believe that the damage was greater from that side, the upper side.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Those photographs can now go?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours those should be marked P1128-26, 27, 28 and 29.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I think it's right that after the shelling finished, troops arrived in the town.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Not when the shelling ended, but when the police, at the end, agreed via a radio station from -- from the car, with the Serb command, for Kozarac to surrender and when they came out under the terms of the surrender and left Kozarac, the police, the wounded persons and the civilians who had found out about it. Only after that did the Serbs enter Kozarac with tanks and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you I think had returned from the temporary clinic to the main clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's correct, when agreement was reached about the surrender and when the others were leaving Kozarac we decided to go back to the clinic because we were aware that a lot of the civilian population, which was hiding either in the basements or in the woods, had no idea that a surrender had been agreed on, and so we thought that if somebody needed any help, that they would come to the clinic, and ask for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, in fact, once you had got back to the clinic, did soldiers arrive?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: After a certain amount of time, not right away, the soldiers did arrive, Serb soldiers, three soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is at page 7740 of the transcript onwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then a JNA lorry and was -- were all your supplies loaded on to that lorry and you were taken by the soldiers to that part of the town, as you marked as the centre?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. Briefly, they first spoke to a Serbian woman, Goga, who was with us the entire time as part of the medical staff, and then Dragan Skrbic who was one of those three soldiers went outside and then I don't know who he talked with, and made an agreement with, but any way, when he came back he said that a military truck would arrive, that we needed to load up all the medicines that were in the clinic, and then when we did that, they escorted us, two by two, to the centre of Kozarac where I wrote that the centre was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think that you and your colleagues were put on to a jeep and taken to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: We waited there for a while. We were standing. And then after a certain amount of time, I must say that we didn't all go to Trnopolje. One soldier came up to Nihad Bahonic. Nihad Bahonic was an ambulance driver who was a professional driver and worked with the ambulance before the war. He asked him for his ID and when he read his name, he told him to go with him. He separated him from us and they went to the north, towards the Kozarac road. When the jeep came to pick us up, I asked what would happen to Bahonic, and one of the soldiers who had a rank, I don't know exactly which rank, said that they would take care of Nihad Bahonic and we went and sat in the jeep and they drove us away. We heard shooting. I think there were only two shots that were fired. I didn't look in that direction. But Azra said that they killed him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Then before we deal with Trnopolje, I'd like to you have a look, please, at a couple of videos that were taken later and which you were shown in the Stakic trial. First of all, could you have a look at -- this is an excerpt, Your Honours, from the video that already had the marking V00-0285. And it was taken from a -- a TV programme called "A town called Kozarac." I wonder if that could be played?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Reporter: There is evidence of what happened along the main road. These are burnt out Muslim homes. Across in a circle is the Serbs way of marking them out for special attention. This is ethnic cleansing with a vengeance and it was thorough. In Prijedor, a few miles --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour excuse me, I object to the sound being played. It's an unknown witness who I can't cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this, we all accept that's TV commentary, there is no reliance or no probative value placed upon that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That acceptable to you, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now it went at some speed but did you recognise, doctor, that road?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I think that this is Prijedor -- the Prijedor-Banja Luka road or rather from Kozarac towards Banja Luka, but the last part was Prijedor, and the road is in fact the Prijedor-Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours may that, then, be made, please, Exhibit P1149?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, could you have a look, please, next at another short exhibit taken from the ABC Nightline programme? And that is V 000-2843. Again, Your Honour, no reliance is placed on the TV reporter's commentary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Reporter: We visited the ethnically cleansed Kozarac in Northern Bosnia last week. We were closely supervised by the local Serb militia restricted to just a few blocks of the town, once home to about 15.000 Muslim men, women, and children?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we stop? Stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I think that this is a building in Kozarac, on the right-hand side Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. as you enter Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should say this was filmed in November of 1992 or rather shortly before that, because that's when the programme went out. Yes, can we carry on?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Reporter: "Today there are no Muslims there, none, and none of their X marked homes is intact. Other homes in Kozarac have been marked to survive. This one with the colours of the Serbian flag. This one says, 'This is Serbia.' They stand undamaged like the remaining Serb residents of Kozarac."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I'm not at all clear why it's all come out black and white because it's in colour but it may be that something went wrong in the copying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, can I move -- thank you, doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could that be made P15 -- 1511 for some reason? Oh, I see. Yes I'm sorry Your Honour I think the gap is because we were just filling up with exhibit numbers. 1511, yes, apparently we've already marked some others.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, from there, were you and your --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: From there, were you and your fellow medical workers taken to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's right. From there, we eventually made it to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Trnopolje part begins on page 7748 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think when you actually arrived, there was no sign that it was any kind of a camp.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The place was milling with military but nobody thought -- it didn't occur to anyone that there were any camps. It was later on that we learned that it was a kind of a camp, but the very beginning, we simply thought that they were taking us in there because of the combat operations and that we would be released.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I think you were there until the very end, virtually, of Trnopolje, as a camp, in September of 1992. You were one of the last people to leave?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's right. On the last day of September, the camp was officially disbanded and on the 1st of October, we turned up in Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you described to the Court in the Stakic trial the various things that happened in Trnopolje, the violence and the rapes that took place. Was the camp itself apparently under the control of the military?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The camp was strictly controlled by the army. It was quite obvious that there were guards at every corner of the camp and the movement was restricted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think you explained how there were sniper posts and machine-gun posts, and in a moment we will have a look at the various diagrams that you drew, but is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It is. And I also said that the military guards guarded the camp changed often. As a rule every three weeks. And then the complete army troops with their armaments also changed. So that it -- which unit would be guarding depended, and the weapons they had, depended on these changes of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in addition to -- I'm sorry, and did the machine-guns in fact face inwards towards the camp?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour this is page 7755.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Of course, not only the machine-guns. All the guard posts faced the camp. Some of them had sandbags in front but they were all facing the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we look, please, at -- I'm sorry, before we look at the diagrams, were you yourself housed in, as it were, a makeshift clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It was the clinic in Trnopolje, in the neighbourhood community, where I used to work before the war. That was my workplace there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you live and sleep in that clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Not before the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, when the camp was in operation.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Of course, I was an inmate like everybody else, but in a way, perhaps we were lucky. That is what it can be called. To be put -- to be put there, to be put in the clinic so that the conditions we lived under were slightly better than those of the rest of the people.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were the people in the clinic who were there with you the veterinarian Azra Blazevic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: They were all with us all the time. Except that one of the next days, Senad Husidic was taken away. At the time when we were crossing from jeep to the buses, they wanted to separate Senad Husidic from us but they let him go on with his family but a few days later they came to Trnopolje, asked for him by name, and took him away, and I heard that he was -- that he had been taken to Omarska. Then towards the end of June, I'm not quite sure when, but I think it was late June or early July, when they came to take away Dr. Jusic Pasic and Dr. Mensur Kusuran, they also asked for them by their names and they took them to Omarska. Dr. Jusuf Pasic was killed in Omarska and Dr. Mensur Kusuran went to Manjaca and there was released from Manjaca and he's still alive today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now in addition to Azra Blazevic was there also a medical student, Vasif Gutic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Vasif Gutic was with us from the outset. He was with us in Kozarac. He had just enrolled medical studies and he was with us in the camp throughout.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we have a look, please, at a series of drawings that you produced? First of all, this one has the number 01035314.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think Mr. Ackerman you've got a whole set of these already.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you just, let's have a look, please, and show us the various parts of this camp. I think first of all, can you show us where the bus that took you to the camp stopped?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The bus which took us to the camp took a village road, fetched up at Trnopolje, then it moved on to this road from Prijedor to Trnopolje. And then the buses fetched up somewhere here more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: There was a dirt road or rather a pedestrian lane, and that -- and down that lane we were taken to the clinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you then, please, let's go through the rest of the matters there. When you -- and you've indicate -- could you indicate, please, on your plan where the clinic was?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: It was here, the entrance was here. This is the yard. This was the neighbourhood community building, a coffee pub, a football pitch. There was a shop in front of it. And the clinic was in between.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you've also indicated a school?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The school was right behind the clinic. It is big elementary school for the first eight grades.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was kept in the school?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: In the school, men were kept, by and large, but it varied. At sometimes there were also women there. The Trnopolje camp had two systems, to all intents and purposes. One was the men's camp, from 17 or 18 to 65 years of age, that is men of military age who were not allowed to leave the camp. And then women, children, and the elderly, who were rounded up in neighbouring villages during the cleansing, and when they would have a sufficient number of them a convoy would be organised and such individuals were then banished from the territory of this Serb Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you indicate to us on this plan, please, where the sniper posts were, first of all?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: From what we could see, it was behind this football pitch, where there was a house and there was a small balcony and a window with a sniper there. And another guard post was down. What we could see, I suppose we could not see everything, but it depended on the guard which kind of weapons they would have. The machine-guns that were there were usually over there. Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you move the plan down slightly because I think it's going off. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Here, at this place, then here, and at times they would also be placed there. But as I've said, it also depended on the guards who were on duty at a particular point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think just for the purposes of the transcript so we need to re-relate it to the plan, you've indicated the circle close to where we can see the ERN number at the top of the plan, then the second one just below the football field, and the third you've indicated at the junction or the crossroads, rather, I should say, of that road. Okay. Can we see to the -- if we look at -- looking at the plan, the right-hand side, can we see the command post indicated?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The command post also shifted from one place to another. In the early days, when the Serb Red Cross came, initially it was then here. For a while, Dr. Ivic, Major Kuruzovic were in the offices here. Then the command post was relocated and Major Kuruzovic then took up a house which was slightly outside the camp, next to the last guard post. And that is where the command post was until the end. That is where Major Kuruzovic spent his time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again just for the purposes of the transcript you indicated that he moved to a house which we can see at the top right-hand part of this plan. Now, can you have a look, please, at a photograph which has already been exhibited, I think? It's marked P1128.1. We will put it up on the ELMO to save -- oh, you've got it right here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, Ms. Korner, this --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, could that be made point 2, 1147.2? That plan?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can you just indicate to us what we can see on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is a camp, I presume it is an aerial photograph, from east to the right, we have the part facing Kozarac. To the left towards the railway tracks. This road here, when you move to the right, it is towards Prijedor, and the other way is Banja Luka. This is here the football, the field. And here you can see the small balcony and the sniper, and the rest of the guards were where this tree is. And then here was the next guard post. And one was next to this house, and one was at the junction over there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is the school. This here is a shop in front of the clinic. This is the entrance to the clinic. The clinic is here. To the left is a room which they used for interrogation and beating of the inmates. This is where you entered the neighbourhood community premises. They had two small rooms there. Here is the coffee shop. Then there is a staircase leading to the football club and here on the side is where you entered this large centre which was not in use yet before the war: This here is the clinic yard. And this is -- you enter the yard first and then the clinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we look, then, next, please, at the sketch plan you did showing the clinic area? That's got the markings 01035316.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that will be P1147.3.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we just very quickly run through that before the break? And perhaps you can just explain to us which was the main part of the clinic?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Well, in point of fact, it is this area here. This is the yard in front of it. This is the entrance. To the left was a room which they used to beat and interrogate people. To the right was a passage way and then there were windows facing the school. Here were the surgeries, that is rooms where we examined patients. Down here was a small larder without windows. This is the neighbourhood community premises with two little rooms and this is the coffee shops above which was the football club. And behind it was a large hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's just have a look at one more photograph, please, and I don't think this has been exhibited yet. It's part of the group. We will put it on the ELMO, 0214-7093. Oh, it has. Oh, it is. It has been exhibited. I gather it's 1128.12. Just put it on the ELMO to make it quicker.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Here we see the clinic again. Its yard, which is here. This is the entrance. These are the three windows of the three surgeries. This is the shop. When you -- as you enter here, to the left is the interrogation room.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, doctor. We've still got five minutes so let's deal with your third sketch plan, please, which is marked 01035317, and will become point 4, P1147.4. Now, it's the same effectively, I think, as the first one you drew but you added something in there. Can you just tell the Court what those crosses are that we can see?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: These crosses indicate that it was after the journalists' visit. Some tents were put up because in the school and the large hall, there wasn't enough room. The inmates put up some makeshift tents, sheets or blankets or something, they somehow improvised some shelters and that is where they slept and spent their time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As the world now knows, there was a massive argument about whether or not there was a barbed wire fence anywhere and I think indeed you testified in the libel trial. First of all, was there a barbed wire fence?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: A wire fence. I think on one side it was barbed. And the other I think it wasn't. But it existed only for a certain period of time, for a relatively short period of time, and it was done with help of inmates who had been brought from Keraterm and Omarska, and after the journalists, after the journalists' visit, the fence was removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the fence was put up, was it, when the prisoners arrived from Omarska and Keraterm, before the visit of the journalists? And then taken down subsequent to the visits of the journalists and the news programmes that went out?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is it possible to see, did you mark on the plan, where that fence was?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No. It's not marked here. I believe I drew another sketch where I did mark it but I can draw it again how it was. It was here, from the big hall towards this fence of the building materials store, and then along the road and ended up here again at the corner of the big hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I tell you what, Your Honour, if Your Honour takes the break we will just identify which sketch it was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes it was drawn in the Stakic case, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's drawn in red. It's marked in red.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right and we will just have to look for that because I seem to have mislaid it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will play it safe. We'll take the break now. You make sure it's there because I could be wrong. We will have a 25 minute break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: My belief that we could finish with this witness today was based upon Ms. Korner's representation that she would finish by the first break. That obviously has not happened. And if you want to make at least provisional arrangements for tomorrow morning at 9.00 that might be wise to do so. We may still finish today but it's less certain at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, before we continue, I inquired about the possibility of tomorrow. There is no possibility of sitting in the morning tomorrow because all the courtrooms are taken. So we will need to sit, we will have to sit in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may have the same problem as Your Honour for a slightly different reason that I have a medical appointment in London tomorrow afternoon, which will mean I would be flying out at 5.00 but Your Honour we will see how things go.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, doctor, can you now have, we found a copy of the one you drew in Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we haven't got enough colour copies to formally place the copy with the Court file for an exhibit but if we can just for the moment identify it and then we will put a copy in tomorrow, a colour copy. Could you have that, please, usher?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the same plan marked 5315 but with your marking. And I think you marked in red where that fence was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The red line is marked and it indicates the fence within which the inmates were when Penny Marshall arrived and this fence was specially constructed, this side, this side, and this side here. The southern side already existed, the southern side of the fence, because that was also the fence to the place where the construction material was kept.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, doctor. That helps and you can take that away. You mentioned when you were describing the camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will be 1147.5.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It will, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think you need to distribute it because we already have it and we can use the one we have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it wasn't distributed Your Honour. We don't actually have a copy -- sorry that's the only one. Usher, could you give that back because we are going to have to recopy that to make that the Court exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned, as I said, major Kuruzovic. Was he, except for the very early part of your stay in the camp in command of the camp throughout?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The first few days when we arrived to the camp, no, he wasn't, but then after a few days, Major Kuruzovic arrived at the camp and then the entire time until the camp was working he was responsible for the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I now want to deal briefly so we can look at the video, with the arrival of the journalists.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the evidence about that began at page 7794 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask you, please, to look at a video -- before we play it, can we pause for a moment? It is excerpts from the full video which I think Your Honours have already seen, plus an excerpt again from the ABC Nightline programme which contains an interview with the witness after his release. So if we could now play that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause for a moment and can we go back again? Just reverse the film? I'm sorry, no, no, reverse the film. All right. Can we start and can we pause when we see the one-armed man?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Doctor, can you tell us who that one-armed man was?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is Mica Kobas. Mica was in Trnopolje together with Dusko Ivic. He's a medical technician, a male nurse, they regularly came to the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I'm so sorry, before we move on because some of the dialogue is indistinct even though it's in English, we did produce a transcript. I'm not sure Your Honours were given it. It may help. And there is one for Mr. Ackerman as well. And Your Honour I rather think on this video we did actually remove some of the commentary, particularly when one sees the -- all right. If we could please play on?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [for text of video, please see draft transcript, Exhibit number 1512.1]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you pause for a moment, please? Your Honour, I should say that this was the return after the first visit. It was some days later when they went back. Again as I say, these are excerpts from various parts of the video. Sorry, yes, can we go on?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we pause, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Doctor, who is the man we can see just behind you?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is Vasif Gutic, a medical student.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can play on, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pause, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that, doctor, is whom?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is Azra Blazevic. She is a veterinarian.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next excerpt is from Nightline.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That's the end of the video. Your Honour, may the video be made P1512 and the transcript in English 1512.1?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, doctor, as everyone knows, you provided to Penny Marshall, a film that contained photographs that you had taken during the time of your incarceration at Trnopolje. And I want you now, please, to look at those photographs and identify them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think Your Honours were given copies of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We had several.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They start with the number 01035330. All right. I think Your Honours have already got these, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's what I thought. Perhaps we can just hand them up one by one in turn. If the whole bundle were to be given an exhibit number together and I'll mark them point 1, point 2, so that would be 1513 and the first one will be point 1. I'll just hand them out as we go. Put them on the ELMO so we can all see what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us that you not only worked at the clinic but slept there. Did you have any beds?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: There were two beds which were at the clinic before, because that was already a clinic before it was a camp, and there were two beds which were used to examine patients. So those were the beds that we found at the clinic when we got there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Who can we see asleep on the top photograph?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Sefik Karabasic is in the top photograph. And Azra Blazevic is on the bottom photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. So that will be -- forgotten the exhibit number again, 1513.1. Thank you. Can we look at the next one marked with the number 331? Thank you. Who do we see there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The midwife is on the top photograph. She slept on one of the beds that was in the clinic. And on the bottom photograph is Vasif Gutic. Behind him you can see Goga. I don't know her last name. She is a Serb who was with us the entire time at Kozarac and for a while also she was at Trnopolje until they forbade her to be with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the bottom photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's just --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, yes, I wasn't listening. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I seem to have --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just checking the notes because there is some confusion. I seem to be missing -- I'm sorry, would Your Honour forgive me?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. It's backwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at this one which is marked 5329? I'm sorry, I forgot. I knew there was some missing. Can you tell us what we are looking at there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Mujo, a male nurse, is on the top photograph. Next to him is a young man who was a patient. I think he spent one night with us. I am on the bottom photograph, behind me is Hase Dzonlagic, he's a veterinarian.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think the camera itself belonged to Dr. Blazevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can that be made point 3?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then could you have a look now please at 10135334? What are we looking at there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The photograph shows the room where the inmates were interrogated and beaten. You can see blood on the walls and on the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next, please, thank you, same room, 33 -- that will be .4. Next one 5335 which will be .5. The same area, I think but taken further back so one can see more of the walls.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's correct. That's the same room and the photograph was taken at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. So that will be .5. Can we be handed -- could you be handed now, together, I think, 5336 and 5337? I think -- well, that's the one that we saw on the film. That shows the injuries to whom?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is Nedzad Jakupovic. He was brought to us from that room because he had an injury on his eye, practically near -- next to his eye and we had to dress this wound. This time, the guard was not standing next to us the whole time. He went outside. And then we decided to photograph this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think as you told the Court in Stakic, all the photographs were taken from the back so as not to alert the people who you were photographing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That is not true. Not so as not to identify who we were photographing. What we were trying to do is to reduce the risk of it being revealed that we were using a camera to photograph in the camp, and that is why we decided, since Nedzad was in such a state, his eyes were swollen, he was not able to see, he was practically knocked out. So we photographed him hoping that he would not notice that we were photographing him because we were afraid that if the Serbs continued to interrogate him and beat him that he would perhaps tell them that we had taken a photograph of him and then we would be in danger. In any case, there was a risk, and we were trying to reduce that risk to the lowest possible level.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we look at the next one briefly, I think there we can see a side view and we can see the injury you spoke about to his eye. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's right. It's the same patient, Nedzad Jakupovic and this photograph was taken at the same time as the other one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be .6 and .7. Now, can we have a look very quickly at a series of photographs taken on the inside of the camp? That will be 38, 39, 40, and 41. Just very quickly can we -- the building we can see at the back, what were we looking at there?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is the shop that sells building and construction material. It's in the background and it's towards the south side, in the direction of the railway station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the next, please?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is looking in the same direction. It's the same building, the shop that sells construction and building material. It was a former shop. So this is the area between the hall and the clinic, and then that room where barbed wire was put up later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the next? Same place?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: The same place, also from the same direction. I don't know who took the photographs. I didn't take these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Finally, 41.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is now more or less taken from the same direction but slightly more to the right, towards the football field, but you cannot see the football field still. To the left is a small shed which is next to the building and construction material shop. To the left, further to the left, is the shop of the -- for the construction material. So this is a view to the right of that. It means that here, before this house is where the Prijedor-Trnopolje-Omarska road lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, doctor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours those will be 8, 9, 10, and 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It we look now, please, at 42 and 43?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't seem to have, Ms. Korner, if you have a spare one, what would be P153.10. We don't have it actually, the three of us. Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The one before the last, .10, yes exactly, we don't have that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know why we haven't got it but we will have to get some more copies done. We have to copy the other plan anyhow so we will arrange that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, 42, please, what are we looking at there, at the back of the tree?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This was taken from the direction of the entrance to the clinic, in the direction of the road, which leads from Trnopolje to Kozarac. The trucks are standing on the road. I think this is a convoy which shortly before the journalists would come, this convoy was organised and a number of the men were allowed to enter and join the convoy. The first convoys that left went by train from the station. Afterwards, I don't know why, it was not possible to go to Doboj. Then they were using trailer trucks covered with tarpaulins and they used the road over Mount Vlasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned that convoys before the journalists came. I think this was right, as you told the Court, this is page 7793, that shortly before the arrival of the journalists, most of the women and children were taken out of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's correct, but I think that for the first -- the first time, some men were released with this first convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can you look, then, please, at the second photograph?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is that same convoy, probably this is the last trailer truck, and inmates who were going inside, you can see one soldier here and one soldier here. They -- the inmates were loaded up into the trailer truck. They were practically one on top of another. The tarpaulins were closed in the summer heat and the inmates were transported like that without water, closed, shut up into these trailer trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours that will be .12 and .13.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And finally the last two photographs which are 344 and 345.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is a man who was in the Trnopolje camp. He had dysentery. He had lost a lot of weight. I think that his name is Hrnic but I'm not sure. He was beaten also on one occasion in that room, and after that, he died. But the reason why he died is probably a consequence of all of that, the fact that he succumbed to dysentery, his body was weakened as a consequence of the beatings and then he died. But I think that the -- that the beating was not the main cause of his death.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he in Trnopolje throughout? Or was he one of the people who came from Omarska or Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: No. He was in Trnopolje, because we took those photographs before the journalists came and then we handed them over. So we had to take them before people from Keraterm and Omarska came.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we just look then again briefly at the second photograph?

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: This is the same man except that we see his lower extremities. You cannot see it here, all that is that you can see is that he is suffering from diarrhoea, all his underwear is wet. We had no medicines to help him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you and that's the final set. That will be 14 and 15. Now then briefly to summarise, the rest of the evidence that you gave, doctor, I think you described first of all killings that took place outside the camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is Your Honours at page 7786. In particular when some people called Foric were taken out of the camp and killed.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: I think that that is how most people were killed. Inmates would be taken out of the Trnopolje camp and killed somewhere. So one day soldiers came with a list and they lined up all male inmates in front of the school and then requested that Forics step out, those whose last flame was Foric. And five or six men came forward and they took them down the road towards the railway station. I'm not sure whether they took them to the fish pond or the old mill but we heard that they had been killed down there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours in due course, they were recovered from a grave, there is exhumation evidence about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that there were?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, is the Prosecutor giving evidence now?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I'm merely pointing out that there will be evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It seems to me that you just testified that they were recovered from a grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, no, I'm anticipating.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I assume there will be somebody I could cross-examine about that at some point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, there will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next I think apart from beatings that took place inside the rooms that you told us about, I think you described beatings that took place in the open. This is at page 7768.

utterances.speaker: IDRIZ MERDZANIC
utterances.text: That's right. For instance, when Keraterm inmates arrived, they were followed by Zigic with another soldier. He entered the area where Keraterm inmates were put up, lined them up, stood in front of them and said, "God help you." He rose, and they were all -- they all then had to respond to this, "God help you." And then he said aloud, "Kum come out" and a man stepped forward from the line. He told him to go down on his knees. He did and then he started beat being him. He beat him with his hands and with his feet until the man fell to the ground.
